environment.working_tree: Modified worktree (50 paths): Products planning/evidence, Catalog adapter/tests and local migrations; no Supabase remote writes or migration applications.

decisions.summary: Catalog adapter selection is explicit local_demo or supabase configuration and fails closed when missing/invalid; ID shape is not used.
Local demo storage is not secure or remotely synchronized; core catalog stores are strict, but product-media stores still use best-effort persistence.
Remote Supabase failures never fall back to local fixtures.
No offline queue or remote mutation replay exists for Products in this release.
Remote Products reads and writes require an online authoritative response; no offline write queue is provided.
Remote Product, cost and media data are not cached for offline reads in this release.
Business lifecycle, connectivity, entity sync state and mutation state remain separate dimensions.
Mutations use expected versions and idempotency; conflicts require explicit resolution and never use last-write-wins.
Local fixture/demo data is never automatically uploaded or merged into remote organization data.
Shared Files, Notes, Activity, Tasks, Relations and Document Intelligence retain their Platform synchronization and recovery boundaries.
Explicit local_demo or supabase adapter selection is implemented; the current runtime lacks VITE_CATALOG_ADAPTER_MODE and therefore fails closed.
Category synchronization and categoryKey migration require reviewed identity, scope and lifecycle mapping.
Costs have no offline cache, queued mutation or replay; reads/writes recheck current server permission.
Gallery order changes only through an online atomic full-gallery command with expected versions; no merge or last-write-wins.
The shared Files ownership boundary is approved; upload/finalization, signed-preview authorization, retention and orphan-recovery semantics remain open.
Asset registration and assignment are separate; an attach failure never deletes a reusable shared Platform File.
Ambiguous cost/media mutations are retried only with the same idempotency key; stale gallery state requires refresh and explicit reconciliation.

actions: Reconciled the earlier sync design against the approved Products API contracts and current cost/media scope.
Verified explicit fail-closed adapter selection and corrected the matrix: core catalog stores are strict, while Product-media stores still use best-effort persistence.
Defined online-only cost access, immediate protected-projection invalidation on permission changes, and no remote cost cache or mutation replay.
Defined atomic manual gallery reordering, same-key retry after ambiguous outcomes, and explicit refresh/reconciliation on order conflicts.
Kept upload, preview, signed URL lifecycle and orphan cleanup in the shared Platform Files boundary; Products does not add a local upload queue or delete a shared File to compensate.
Expanded migration, user-visible recovery and multiplatform test cases for costs, media assignments, file upload, previews and gallery ordering.

Revalidated against access attempt 11 and API attempt 11: shared Files and audit semantics are approved, while media-table/preview lifecycle enforcement and Products audit atomicity evidence remain open.

validation.evidence: All 34 delivery state-machine and evidence tests passed.
Delivery ledger validation passed: 8 ledger(s) checked.
Module run validation passed: 110 checkpoint files checked (36 archived legacy records).

validation.command: Review sync-model.md against current Product stores, adapters, access and API contracts
validation.evidence: Explicit mode, strict catalog persistence, best-effort media persistence, shared Files ownership, audit requirements and remote-write gates match current evidence.

requirements.evidence: The online-only target and explicit fail-closed mode are documented; runtime configuration is absent, and versions/idempotency are not implemented. Core catalog persistence is strict, but media stores remain best-effort.
No-cache/no-replay behavior and permission invalidation are specified; current cost permission/RLS and adapter enforcement remain insufficient.
Atomic order, retry and failure recovery are specified; the shared Files boundary is approved, but media lifecycle/table enforcement and current assignment version/order fields remain open or absent.
Migration remains gated on actual category inventory, approved mapping and category implementation.
Stable catalog_item references are preserved; Products does not duplicate CRM identity or Platform synchronization.
One semantic online-only policy and recovery contract is defined; desktop/mobile runtime evidence is absent and iOS/Android are deferred.

evidence.result: Defines state dimensions, local/remote storage boundaries, operation matrix, no-queue policy, retries, conflicts, migration/recovery and media/cost tests.
Catalog adapter requires VITE_CATALOG_ADAPTER_MODE=local_demo or supabase and rejects missing/invalid configuration.
Generic storage defaults to best-effort, while core catalog stores use strict persistence; Product-media stores currently retain the best-effort default.
Current media adapter writes directly to Storage and platform_files, creates an ERP asset in the same method, removes shared resources during cleanup and generates signed URLs directly.
Local media upload uses shared local Files but pairs file creation and ERP asset creation, with direct file removal on asset failure.
Defines no offline replay, idempotent retries, cost permission gates, same-organization Files references and atomic full-gallery order.
Shared Files boundary and append-only audit semantics are approved; media metadata enforcement, full deployed ERP RLS and Products audit atomicity remain open.
Core catalog stores use strict persistence; Product-media asset and assignment stores use createLocalStore's best-effort default.
Product Owner confirmed manual ordering for each product/SKU media gallery.

detected_failure.summary: Product-media stores can suppress persistence failures, and the remote media adapter owns direct upload/metadata/cleanup/signed-URL operations rather than delegating finalized-file lifecycle to shared Platform Files.

likely_failure_origin.phase: prior implementation before approved shared Files and sync contracts
likely_failure_origin.rationale: Current media adapters combine file and ERP asset lifecycle and lack order/version recovery; exact originating changes are not established.

next_handoff: 06-plan: sequence media persistence/Files integration, audit atomicity, cost/RLS and configuration tasks; keep remote writes and migration blocked until deployed-state and authorized legacy-data evidence pass.
notes: No code, schema, migration, runtime data or remote database was changed in this phase.

The shared Files boundary and append-only audit semantics are approved; remote writes remain blocked on media lifecycle/table enforcement, Products audit atomicity, forward RLS/permission migrations, deployed-state verification and authorized legacy-data dry run.
No remote offline cache or mutation queue is approved; local demo fixtures must never be presented as remote data.
Manual gallery order is approved, but current persistence lacks position/version fields and must be planned as an atomic migration/command.
User-approved mobile web scope is covered by the same semantic contracts; native iOS/Android remain deferred.
